title: Tiered open/close scheduler with tranche-based fallback strategy for dependency circuits
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Background: We need a robust circuit-breaker system that operates per dependency, per model variant, and per tenant to protect SLOs and enable safe progressive degradation across regions. Current simple fuses either trip too aggressively or fail to provide smooth recoveries. Goal: implement a tiered scheduler that opens/closes circuits on tranche windows, supports exponential backoff and half-open probes, and orchestrates tranche-based fallbacks (model variant downgrade, regional redirection, and cached-response serving) while preserving correctness for multi-tenant routing and SLO accounting.
success_criteria: P99 tail latency for host-critical routes remains within 10% of baseline under 3x traffic spikes using fallback chain
Automated canary shows >90% successful fallback routing with no customer-facing errors in beta customers
No unplanned cross-tenant degradation during fault injection tests in staging
Dashboards show correct attribution of failures and fallback events by tenant, model, and region
implementation_notes: Circuit granularity: dependency endpoint (e.g., model-serving:embed-v1), model variant (quantized vs full), and tenant; each circuit holds independent metrics and state
Tranche windows: scheduler operates in 30s tranches with a 3-tranche grace window (90s) to avoid flip-flopping; configurable per route
Trip rule (default): error_rate >= 5% AND p95_latency >= 2x SLO over 3 of last 6 tranches => open circuit

Backoff policy: on open, schedule exponential backoff for next half-open probe (initial wait 30s, multiplier 2, max 1h). Half-open sends N probe requests (default 10) evenly across the tranche to test recovery

Fallback chain: 1) same-architecture quantized variant, 2) cheaper but compatible model (e.g., smaller context), 3) cached prefix/KV response, 4) synthetic deprecation response with safe error code and Retry-After header
Per-tenant weight: tenants can opt a 'safety profile' that tightens trip thresholds (e.g., error_rate threshold to 2%) or relaxes them for low-SLA internal tenants

Regional handling: when a dependency circuit trips in a region, scheduler consults global routing policy to (a) redirect to healthy region if latency delta < configured threshold, or (b) enter local graceful degradation path
State persistence: circuit state is persisted to distributed state store with TTL slightly larger than max backoff to survive controller restarts; store keys are namespaced by cluster/region
Observability: emit events for TRANCHE_OPEN, TRANCHE_PROBE, TRANCHE_CLOSE, FALLBACK_TRIGGER with tags: tenant, model_id, dependency, region, reason, sample_request_id
Interaction with KV cache: when a model fallback occurs to a cached response, emitter tags include cache-key and cache-hit=true; ensure cache TTL aligns with privacy rules
test_plan: Unit tests: scheduler state machine (open/half-open/closed) and backoff timing determinism
Integration: staging multi-region deploy with chaos tests that inject latency and error bursts to dependency endpoints
Load tests: synthetic traffic scaled to 4x production baseline to validate tranche stability and fallback chain behavior
Failure-mode tests: ensure tenant isolation by simulating noisy neighbor hitting a model until it trips and verifying other tenants unaffected
Canary: internal canary with 5% of traffic + opt-in beta customers; monitor rollback metrics for 60 minutes before progressive ramp
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: Circuit Overview panel - active circuits, open duration histogram, per-tenant counts
SLO-derived alerts: fire when fallback rate for critical routes > 1% sustained for 10 minutes
Pager: pager if multi-region redirect rate > 10% for core model families and user-visible error rate > 0.5%
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - alpha: internal infra + platform tests only, feature-flag on. Duration: 2 weeks
Phase 2 - beta: enable for non-critical tenant cohorts and internal services (5% traffic). Monitor and collect telemetry for 2 weeks
Phase 3 - staged customer ramp: enable by tenant cohorts with daily ramps and automated rollback if key metrics regress
Phase 4 - global enable: remove tight flags, keep soft alerts and long-term monitoring
Kill switch: global opt-out via config that immediately forces circuits closed and disables fallbacks; documented in runbook

estimated_risks: Incorrect thresholds could either trip too often and cause unnecessary fallbacks or be too lax and allow SLO violations
State store availability is critical; misconfiguration may lead to inconsistent circuit state across regions
Cross-tenant caching bugs could leak data if namespace enforcement fails
Regional redirect decisions may increase tail latency for some customers if not bounded by latency delta thresholds
follow_up_tasks: Add per-route ML-derived threshold tuner to propose trip thresholds based on historical SLO breach patterns (future work)
Formalize per-tenant SLA profiles and expose config in Console for SREs and customer success
Add advanced simulation harness to run randomized fault traces across model variants and tenants
Post-mortem template: include breakdown of circuit events, fallback chain, and tenant impact for any production incident
